system.name: HALO (heterogeneous-agent Lyapunov policy optimization)
system.one_liner: MARL framework for human-robot collaboration that projects decentralized policy gradients onto a Lyapunov-stable direction so the rationality gap contracts monotonically.

content.variant_note: an upper layer of environment, agents and real-world deployment hands signals down to a grey band of boxed equations, whose result returns as the final parameter update
content.argues: Decentralized agents trained on conflicting gradients can be stabilised by a short analytic chain (rationality gap, stability normal vector, closed-form projection) that rectifies their update and carries over to real-world collaboration.
content.subject: Centralized-training, decentralized-execution agents in a collaboration scene, and the equation chain of Lyapunov policy optimization.

elements.name: Centralized training
elements.role: names the long black line that leaves the interaction space and reaches the agents with s and r = R(s, a)
elements.drawn_as: label set into a thick black line over the top of the figure

elements.name: Infinite interaction space

elements.name: Agent i
elements.role: one decentralized learner: state s_i gives observation o_i, policy outputs action a_i
elements.drawn_as: peach band holding a state box s_i and a policy box π_θi(a_i|o_i)

elements.name: Agent j
elements.role: second learner, same structure; '… …' between the bands stands for more agents
elements.drawn_as: peach band with s_j and π_θj(a_j|o_j) boxes

elements.name: Decentralized execution
elements.role: each agent sends only its own action a_i, a_j to the environment
elements.drawn_as: serif label between the interaction space and the agent bands

elements.name: Lyapunov policy optimization (grey band)
elements.role: holds the proposed update rule as a chain of equation boxes
elements.drawn_as: full-width grey band with bold title at top left

elements.name: Differentiable gradient fields
elements.role: holds the two gradient fields u_ind(θ) (Independent rationality) and u_team(θ) (Team rationality)
elements.drawn_as: light-blue box with blue title and two white rounded boxes with captions

elements.name: Lyapunov rationality gap
elements.role: V(θ) = ½‖u_ind(θ) − u_team(θ)‖², the gap between independent and team gradients
elements.drawn_as: white square box with name above the formula

elements.name: Stability normal vector
elements.role: h = (H_ind − H_team)ᵀ(u_ind − u_team), obtained from the gap by a Hessian-vector product
elements.drawn_as: white square box with name above the formula

elements.name: Lyapunov-constrained optimization
elements.role: argmin over d of ½‖d − u_ind(θ)‖², with a bowl graphic at the box's right end
elements.drawn_as: white square box with name above the formula

elements.name: Analytic closed-form projection
elements.role: closed-form multiplier λ* and projected direction d* = u_ind − λ*h, reached through the KKT condition
elements.drawn_as: white square box with name above the formulas

elements.name: Hessian-vector product / KKT condition
elements.role: name the two derivation steps on the arrows between equation boxes
elements.drawn_as: plain serif labels beside an upward and a downward arrow

elements.name: Final parameter update
elements.role: the projected update goes back to the agents' policies
elements.drawn_as: brown label beside a double-line upward arrow

elements.name: Policy
elements.role: the learned policy is carried to the real-world collaboration
elements.drawn_as: label above a double-line arrow pointing to the photo

evidence: The HALO framework architecture combining the transition from standard decentralized learning to Lyapunov policy optimization for real-world HRC.
We design a stability-aware control law that rectifies decentralized gradients to satisfy a convergence certificate, as illustrated in Fig. 1.

summary: HALO (heterogeneous-agent Lyapunov policy optimization) stabilises decentralized multi-agent RL for human-robot collaboration by projecting each agent's gradient so that the rationality gap between independent and team objectives contracts. Figure 1 is a two-layer system diagram. The upper layer shows centralized training and decentralized execution: an 'Infinite interaction space' box with a collaboration versus interference scene, two peach agent bands with state and policy boxes exchanging actions and states, and a real-world photo of a robot and a human carrying a beam under a motion-capture truss. A full-width grey band beneath chains boxed equations: gradient fields, rationality gap, stability normal vector, a constrained optimisation with a small bowl graphic, and the closed-form projection, whose result returns as the final parameter update.
